newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn and soybean condition ratings decline.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn and soybean condition ratings decline.

text.p: Condition ratings for Ohio's corn and soybean crops declined last week amid minimal rainfall and cooler-than-desired temperatures, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.
The corn crop as of Sunday was rated 38 percent good to excellent, down from 41 percent in that category the previous week.
Eleven percent of the crop was in the dent stage of development, below 51 percent a year ago and below the 54 percent average pace.
The weekly crop brief showed 37 percent of the soybean crop rated good to excellent, down from 42 percent the previous week.
Eighty-four percent of the soybean crop was setting pods, lagging 100 percent a year ago and below the average of 100 percent.
Topsoil moisture levels were 22 percent very short, 47 percent short and 31 percent adequate.
The state's pastures were 26 percent good to excellent, down from 31 percent the previous week.
